title: Adaptive seed tutorials and empty-canvas skeletons for Console onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a set of adaptive 'seed tutorials' and empty-canvas skeletons for the Redwood Console. These are micro-educational experiences that appear in contextual locations (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost views) and adapt to inferred user intent (first-time explorer, billing-conscious admin, rollout engineer). Goal: reduce time-to-first-success (TTFS) and increase setup completion for new accounts while avoiding clutter for returning power users.
background: Current first-touch surfaces rely on static cards and long walkthroughs. Research from last quarter (usability 2025-Q4) showed users drop off when the initial setup requires too many choices. We want a progressive, adaptive approach: start with a minimal skeleton that seeds the console with curated templates and small, reversible actions. This ticket covers the design deliverables, prototype testing, and developer handoff artifacts.
hypothesis: If we replace one-size-fits-all onboarding cards with adaptive seed tutorials and contextual empty-canvas scaffolds, then new users will complete critical setup tasks 25% faster and D1 retention of playground usage will increase by 15%.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype covering Dashboard, Rollouts, and Cost views with three adaptive states (novice, guided, compact).
Clickable prototype tested in 5 moderated sessions with target personas and summarized results in the ticket comments.
Design tokens and behavior spec ready for frontend (states, transitions, telemetry hooks, A/B flags).
Accessibility checklist completed (keyboard focus, screen reader labels, color contrast).
Implementation proposal and a PR template linked for engineering handoff.
tasks: Map current empty states and identify three high-impact surfaces
Create low-fi flows for adaptive branching and outline telemetry triggers
Design hi-fi cards and skeletons in Figma with tokenized components
Prototype interactions and micro-animations for progressive disclosure
Run moderated usability sessions (5 participants) and synthesize findings
Update Console component library with new EmptyCanvas component spec
Write frontend acceptance tests and QA checklist
Prepare rollout experiment plan and success metrics
metrics_and_experiment_plan: Primary metric: Time-to-first-success (TTFS) for dashboard setup
Secondary metric: D1 playground usage retention
Guardrail: No increase in support tickets tagged 'onboarding confusion'
Experiment buckets: control (existing cards), adaptive-lite, adaptive-full
Sample size target: 1,200 new accounts over 4 weeks
usability_summary: Session 01-05 moderated with product managers and developers acting as proxy users
Key findings: users liked reversible micro-actions, confusion around cost cards persisted if verbosity was high
Action: collapse verbose cost tips into an on-demand drawer and add an 'Explain my bill' quickflow
Design tweak: increase CTA contrast and add onboarding dismiss persistence to avoid repeated prompts
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: default to 'guided' state for orgs with <3 API calls/day; allow experienced users to opt into compact mode
Tradeoff: showing rollout templates inline speeds setup but risks cluttering the initial dashboard—mitigated by progressive reveal based on usage signals
Decision: initial telemetry will be coarse (event names + boolean flags) to reduce privacy overhead; product will reassess after 6 weeks
qa_checklist: Keyboard navigable: all CTAs reachable and visible focus state
Screen reader: descriptive aria-labels for seed actions
Localization: text placeholders available for EU and APAC locales
Performance: skeleton load under 200ms on 3G simulated network
Telemetry: events fire for show/hide, action click, dismiss, and completion
